title: Cold rebuild: Block insert
summary: Rebuild Block insert from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Block insert** in *Undo, dot, registers and visual mode*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: You pressed `dd` five times and deleted one line too many. Which is the quickest correct fix?
steps.explain: Each `dd` is its own change, so one `u` brings back the last line. `p` would paste it below the cursor, possibly in the wrong place.

steps.title: Rebuild Block insert cold
prompt: Model block-visual insert and delete. Write:

- `List<string> BlockInsert(List<string> lines, int top, int bottom, int col, string text)`: for rows `top..bottom` inclusive, insert `text` at column `col`. Lines shorter than `col` are left unchanged (that is what vim's `I` does).
- `List<string> BlockDelete(List<string> lines, int top, int bottom, int left, int right)`: for rows `top..bottom`, delete columns `left..right` inclusive, only the part of each line that exists.
Other rows are untouched. Do not modify the input list.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<string> BlockInsert(List<string> lines, int top, int bottom, int col, string text)
List<string> BlockDelete(List<string> lines, int top, int bottom, int left, int right)
